sources.name: dqnamo
sources.holds: A design engineer's portfolio of interface experiments.
sources.notes: Link only. No terms, no licence, and a public repo with no LICENSE file, so it is all rights reserved.

sources.name: DVIDS
sources.holds: US military media.
sources.notes: US Government works with conditions. Commercial use needs a disclaimer and obscured markings.

sources.name: ElevenLabs Music
sources.holds: Hosted AI music on paid plans.
sources.notes: The free plan has no downloads or API. Film, TV, radio and studio games need Enterprise.

sources.name: European Space Agency
sources.holds: Space imagery and video from ESA.
sources.exclude_reason: Commercial use needs written permission. Only some items carry CC BY-SA.

sources.name: Excalidraw libraries
sources.holds: Hand-drawn shape libraries from the community.
sources.notes: The site says all are MIT, while at least one entry notes other terms. Check each library's note.

sources.name: Exolyt
sources.holds: TikTok analytics with CSV exports.
sources.exclude_reason: Its terms ban systematic extraction, including by script.

sources.name: fal.ai
sources.holds: Hosted video, image and 3D models, paid per use.
sources.notes: Behind Altocue's spend gate. Uploads sit on a public link until they expire.

sources.name: Fancy Components
sources.holds: The strongest kinetic type of the React libraries.
sources.notes: Would need a port to a seekable clock.

sources.name: ffmpeg xfade
sources.holds: 58 named transitions built into ffmpeg.
sources.notes: Part of ffmpeg, which Altocue already needs.

sources.name: Flickr Commons
sources.holds: Heritage photographs from libraries and archives.
sources.notes: No known copyright restrictions, but no warranty. A commercial key may carry fees, and storage limits apply.

sources.name: Fluent Emoji
sources.holds: A full open emoji set.

sources.name: Fluent Emoji Animated
sources.holds: Animated emoji as 256 pixel animated PNGs.
sources.notes: About 5 GB in Git LFS, so take single files only.

sources.name: Fontshare
sources.holds: A hundred fonts under two different licences.
sources.notes: 64 fonts sit under a licence that bars shipping them in an application and bars subsetting. The other 36 are OFL. People may fetch them for themselves.

sources.name: Fontsource
sources.holds: More than 2,000 open fonts as direct files.
sources.notes: Mostly OFL. Usually keep the notice.

sources.name: framecn
sources.holds: A small free set of video components built on Editframe.
sources.notes: 15 free items are MIT, 68 Pro items are paid. The Editframe licence was not verified.

sources.name: Free Music Archive
sources.holds: Curated music with a licence on every track.
sources.notes: Anything marked FMA-Limited is personal listening only. Downloads appear to need a sign-in.

sources.name: FreePD
sources.holds: A public domain music site, now closed.
sources.exclude_reason: The site says it closed permanently in 2025.

sources.name: Freesound
sources.holds: A huge community sound library with a licence on every sound.

access.rate_limit: 60 per minute and 2,000 per day. Originals 30 per minute and 500 per day through OAuth2

sources.notes: Default to CC0 and CC BY. Its API terms say commercial use is negotiated and may be charged later, and bar full copies.

sources.name: GL Transitions
sources.holds: Open GLSL transitions, each a pure function of progress.

credit.template: Keep the header in the shader

sources.notes: Each one needs both clips, so it belongs in the picture edit. Only MIT and BSD items are listed.

sources.name: glTF-Transform
sources.holds: Shrinks and repairs GLB files.

sources.name: G'MIC colour presets
sources.holds: More than 1,100 colour lookup tables.
sources.notes: The licence of the table files is not clear from the page.

sources.name: Google Fonts repository
sources.holds: The open fonts behind Google Fonts, with a licence per family.
sources.notes: Fonts with a Reserved Font Name cannot keep that name once subset, so check before subsetting. The hosted API needs a key, the git repo does not.

sources.name: cedeber/hald-clut
sources.holds: HaldCLUTs including sets derived from commercial products.
sources.exclude_reason: Tagged GPL-3.0, which is doubtful for sets derived from commercial products.

sources.name: Hero Patterns
sources.holds: Repeating SVG background patterns.

sources.name: Higgsfield
sources.holds: Hosted video and image generation with recipes for reels.
sources.notes: Behind Altocue's spend gate. Terms changed on 23 October 2026: output may not pass as human made, and uploads may train its models without an Enterprise Agreement. Uploading a project's footage stays off by default.

sources.name: Hover.css
sources.holds: CSS hover effects.
sources.exclude_reason: Commercial use needs a paid licence.

sources.name: html-video
sources.holds: HTML video templates with the best manifest design we found.
sources.notes: Last pushed in June 2026.

sources.name: Humaaans
sources.holds: Mix-and-match CC0 illustrated people.

sources.name: Hyper3D Rodin
sources.holds: Hosted 3D generation with an API on its Business plan.
sources.notes: Its terms were not read, only its pricing page.

sources.name: HyperFrames registry
sources.holds: Hundreds of seekable motion blocks made for the renderer Altocue uses.

credit.template: Keep the licence files that come with the item

sources.notes: Fetched item by item through `altocue library add`. Most run GSAP, which is under GreenSock's standard licence, not an open one. Branded items and transitions.dev ports are refused.

sources.name: Iconify
sources.holds: One API over hundreds of open icon sets.
sources.notes: Use an allow-list. Block CC BY-NC, GPL sets and ri. Treat simple-icons and logos as trademarks even though they read CC0.

sources.name: IconScout
sources.holds: An animated icon marketplace.
sources.exclude_reason: Its licence page turned away every read, so nothing could be verified.

sources.name: Incompetech
sources.holds: Kevin MacLeod's music, free with a fixed credit line.

credit.template: {title} by Kevin MacLeod, CC BY 4.0, incompetech.com

sources.notes: A paid no-credit licence also exists. Automated download is not addressed in its terms.

sources.name: Internet Archive
sources.holds: A vast archive of films, with rights set by whoever uploaded them.
sources.notes: A person must check every item. Its public domain tag sits on recent feature films, so a machine cannot trust it.

sources.name: ISF Files
sources.holds: Open interactive shader format files.
sources.notes: Skip stateful multi-pass shaders, which cannot seek.

sources.name: Isoflow
sources.holds: An isometric diagram editor.
sources.notes: Open core, and its icon pack licence varies. An editor, not a timed animation.

sources.name: IWLTBAP
sources.holds: Free LUTs from a small publisher.
sources.exclude_reason: No licence text was found on its pages.

sources.name: Jamendo
sources.holds: A Creative Commons music catalogue.
sources.exclude_reason: Its API is free only for non-commercial use and bars offline caching.

sources.name: KayKit
sources.holds: CC0 stylised 3D packs.
sources.notes: CC0 per its listings on itch.io and OpenGameArt.

sources.name: Kenney
sources.holds: CC0 game assets: sound effects, jingles, 3D kits and characters.
sources.notes: Altocue already ships some of its sound effects. Credit the name if you credit anything, and never use the logo. Its isometric packs are 2D tiles.

sources.name: Kokonut UI
sources.holds: A free MIT set of 102 animated components.
sources.notes: The MIT free set only, hand-ported to a seekable clock. Its Pro set is paid and barred from open source, so take names from /r/registry.json and never from llms.txt.

sources.name: lemo-opuscar
sources.holds: Excellent style prompts with demo source code, not an asset library.

credit.template: Keep the MIT notice for any code, credit the films

sources.notes: Link plus patterns. Code and guides are MIT, the demo films are CC BY 4.0, and archive footage in them is not ours to ship. We learn from it and write our own.

sources.name: Library of Congress
sources.holds: Historic film, video and photographs from the US national library.

access.rate_limit: 20 per minute, with a one hour block

sources.notes: The library says it generally does not own the rights. The API answered 403 from a bot check, so nothing here was tested.

sources.name: Lordicon
sources.holds: Animated icons behind an account.
sources.exclude_reason: Its free tier forbids derivatives, and a graphic in a video edit is one.

sources.name: lottie-web
sources.holds: The player for Lottie animation files.
sources.notes: A player only, for files you own.

sources.name: LottieFiles
sources.holds: The largest library of free Lottie animations.
sources.exclude_reason: Its licence allows commercial use while its terms call the free plan strictly non-commercial, and robots are barred.

sources.name: Lucide
sources.holds: Clean open line icons.
sources.notes: ISC sits outside the bundle rule, so it is fetched, not shipped.

sources.name: lucide-animated
sources.holds: 468 animated icons for React.
sources.notes: Selected icons could be ported to plain SVG with the notice kept.

sources.name: LYGIA
sources.holds: A shader library under a commercial-trial licence.
sources.exclude_reason: Prosperity licence, with only a 30-day commercial trial for a whole company.

sources.name: Magic UI
sources.holds: Animated components for React.
sources.notes: Would need a port to a seekable clock. Its Pro terms were not read.

sources.name: Mapbox GL JS
sources.holds: A map renderer that went proprietary at version 2.
sources.exclude_reason: Proprietary since version 2, and it needs a key.

sources.name: MapLibre GL JS
sources.holds: An open map renderer.

sources.name: Mazwai
sources.holds: A former stock site that now redirects to Freepik.
sources.exclude_reason: It now redirects to Freepik, whose terms bar robots and machine learning.

sources.name: Meshy
sources.holds: Hosted text and image to 3D.
sources.notes: The free plan is CC BY 4.0 with no API. Paid plans are customer owned.

sources.name: Microsoft Rocketbox
sources.holds: Rigged human avatars in an archived repo.
sources.notes: Size not checked.

sources.name: Mixamo
sources.holds: Rigged characters and animation behind an Adobe sign-in.
sources.exclude_reason: It needs an Adobe sign-in, bars raw file distribution and bars machine learning.

sources.name: Mixkit
sources.holds: Free music, sound effects and clips from Envato.
sources.exclude_reason: Its terms bar aggregating items, building a competitive product and using bots for download.

sources.name: Motion Primitives
sources.holds: A small set of motion components for React.

sources.name: MotionSites
sources.holds: A paid library of AI website prompts.
sources.exclude_reason: Its terms bar republishing or scraping the library, and the grant covers websites and apps, not video.

sources.name: MusicGen weights
sources.holds: AI music weights under a non-commercial licence.
sources.exclude_reason: The weights are CC BY-NC 4.0, so nothing made with them can be used commercially.

sources.name: Musopen
sources.holds: Recordings of classical music.
sources.exclude_reason: Its FAQ turned away every read, so its terms could not be verified.

sources.name: NASA Images and Video
sources.holds: Agency video, photographs and audio from NASA's public library.
sources.notes: No key and real MP4 files. Manifest URLs are plain http, so rewrite them. Reject items that mention copyright or courtesy, because third-party media is marked only in the text. Never imply endorsement.

sources.name: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio
sources.holds: Science visualisations from NASA.
sources.notes: The search works. File addresses were not tested. Third-party data is possible, so check each item.

sources.name: Natural Earth
sources.holds: Public domain vector and raster base maps.
sources.notes: Some embedded third-party data is licensed only for making a world base map.

sources.name: Noto animated emoji
sources.holds: 881 animated emoji as Lottie files.
sources.notes: CC BY 4.0 by third-party report only. Google's page states no licence, so hold back until it is confirmed.

sources.name: Noto Emoji
sources.holds: An open emoji font and image set.
sources.notes: The fonts are OFL. Tools and most images are Apache-2.0.

sources.name: National Park Service
sources.holds: Park video from the US National Park Service.

access.rate_limit: 1,000 per hour with a free key

sources.notes: Generally public domain, with third-party parts excepted. Credit is appreciated, not required.

sources.name: Open Doodles
sources.holds: A small CC0 set of sketched illustrations.

sources.name: Open Peeps
sources.holds: A hand-drawn CC0 people library.
sources.notes: A DiceBear style can generate them in code.

sources.name: Open Props
sources.holds: Easing and motion tokens as CSS variables.

sources.name: OpenColorIO ACES config
sources.holds: Standard ACES colour configurations.

sources.name: OpenFreeMap
sources.holds: Free hosted OpenStreetMap tiles.

access.rate_limit: No view caps. Offline at most 3,000 tiles or 50 MB, 4 at a time

sources.notes: Credit is needed, including in video.

sources.name: OpenGameArt
sources.holds: Game audio and art with a licence on every asset.
sources.notes: Mixes CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA and GPL, so check each asset.

sources.name: OpenMoji
sources.holds: An open emoji set with a share-alike licence.
sources.notes: Share-alike reaches what you make with it.

sources.name: OpenStreetMap
sources.holds: Global map data made by volunteers.
sources.notes: The data is fine. The public tiles bar offline and bulk use.

sources.name: Openverse
sources.holds: A search index over openly licensed images and audio. It has no video.
sources.notes: Search hung on 21 of 21 tries, while its status pages answered. Treat it as a fallback until it answers, with an 8 second timeout.

sources.name: OutlierKit
sources.holds: YouTube outlier research on paid plans.
sources.notes: One of its comparison pages was wrong, so distrust its comparisons.

sources.name: Paper Shaders
sources.holds: Zero-dependency canvas shaders with a frame control for seeking.

sources.name: Paper Animator
sources.holds: A paid browser tool for paper-style animation.
sources.notes: Link only. Its terms forbid copying service content without written consent. Altocue's paper formats are original.

sources.name: Pexels
sources.holds: Free stock video and photos.
sources.notes: New API keys are paused, so only people who already hold a key can use this route.

sources.name: Phosphor Icons
sources.holds: A flexible open icon family.

sources.name: Pixabay
sources.holds: Free stock video, photos, illustrations and vectors.

access.rate_limit: 100 per 60 seconds. Results must be cached for 24 hours

sources.notes: The best route for generic B-roll. The API asks you to show the source in results. Its terms bar scraping, bulk use and collecting data for machine learning.

sources.name: Pixabay Music
sources.holds: Free music with no documented API.
sources.notes: A person downloads it by hand. Its terms bar robots.

sources.name: Pixabay Sound Effects
sources.holds: Free sound effects with no documented API.
sources.notes: A person downloads it by hand. Its terms bar robots.

sources.name: Mint
sources.holds: A 3D generation service for agents, with a gallery of experiences.
sources.notes: On your own account only, and prices show only after sign-in. Mint assigns you what it holds in your own output. Assets from other people's experiences are not licensed, and some gallery pieces show third-party characters. Its repo code is MIT, its CDN assets are not.

sources.name: Poly Haven
sources.holds: CC0 textures, HDRIs and 3D models.
sources.notes: The live API needs a unique User-Agent and must say the assets came from Poly Haven. Its look is photoreal.

sources.name: Pond5 public domain
sources.holds: A public domain collection reported only second hand.
sources.exclude_reason: Its licence page turned away every read, so nothing about it could be verified.

sources.name: Prompt Motion
sources.holds: A curated gallery of motion made by coding agents, shown with the prompts behind it.
sources.notes: Link only. It has no terms page, so everything is all rights reserved, and each item belongs to its maker.

sources.name: Protomaps
sources.holds: A daily world map build read by range requests.
sources.notes: The world build is 139 GB, so take extracts and never download it whole.

sources.name: Q-DDL LUT pack
sources.holds: A pack of more than 800 LUTs known mainly from 2020 press.
sources.notes: CC BY by press report only. Downloads run through ad-link shorteners.

sources.name: Quaternius
sources.holds: CC0 low-poly 3D packs.
sources.notes: No API and a mixed look, so a person picks.

sources.name: RawTherapee HaldCLUT
sources.holds: A film simulation set.
sources.exclude_reason: The page returned 404, so its licence could not be verified.

sources.name: React Bits
sources.holds: A large set of animated React components.
sources.exclude_reason: MIT with Commons Clause. It bars redistribution alone, in a bundle or as a port.

sources.name: Ready Player Me
sources.holds: An avatar service reported closed.
sources.exclude_reason: Reported shut down on 31 January 2026, by secondary sources.

sources.name: Remix Icon
sources.holds: An icon set that moved to a custom licence in January 2026.
sources.notes: Bars competing libraries and logos. Iconify's metadata still lists it as Apache-2.0.

sources.name: Remocn
sources.holds: Frame-pure motion components for Remotion.
sources.notes: Patterns only until ported. It needs Remotion, which Altocue does not use.

sources.name: Remotion
sources.holds: A popular framework for video in React.
sources.exclude_reason: Source-available, with a company licence above its free tier, so Altocue takes no dependency on it.

sources.name: Rhubarb Lip Sync
sources.holds: A tool that turns speech into mouth shapes for animation.

sources.name: Rive Marketplace
sources.holds: Community animation files under CC BY.
sources.notes: HyperFrames has no Rive adapter, so these do not reach a render today.

sources.name: rough.js
sources.holds: Hand-drawn lines and shapes in code.

sources.name: Sandcastles
sources.holds: Reels, TikTok and Shorts outlier research.
sources.notes: It takes a licence over user content to train AI, so warn before connecting it.

sources.name: Scott Buckley
sources.holds: Cinematic music free with credit, about 280 tracks by estimate.
sources.notes: No API. A person picks and downloads.

sources.name: shadcn registry directory
sources.holds: A live list of component registries with health scores.
sources.notes: A discovery feed, not a licence. Each registry needs its own check.

sources.name: Shadertoy
sources.holds: A vast community of shaders.
sources.exclude_reason: Shaders default to a non-commercial, share-alike licence, and its terms page could not be read.

sources.name: Smithsonian Open Access
sources.holds: CC0 records and images across the Smithsonian's museums.
sources.notes: The CC0 counts come from its live stats API, because the FAQ turned away the read. A video filter returned nothing, so treat this as photos only.

sources.name: snapcn
sources.holds: Frame-pure motion components for Remotion.
sources.notes: Patterns only until ported.

sources.name: Social Blade
sources.holds: Public channel statistics across platforms, sold as prepaid credits.
sources.notes: Its terms were not read.

sources.name: Sonniss GDC bundles
sources.holds: About 207 GB of professional sound effects across yearly bundles.
sources.notes: Royalty free in finished work. It may not be redistributed as sound effects, and AI use is strictly barred.

sources.name: Spline
sources.holds: A visual 3D design tool.
sources.exclude_reason: GUI first, export is paid, and its runtime package has no licence field or LICENSE file.

sources.name: Spyglass
sources.holds: A creative search engine with hook text for Instagram, TikTok and Meta ads.
sources.notes: Your own key, business use only, with hard row caps. Its API has no YouTube, despite the homepage.

sources.name: Stable Audio Open
sources.holds: A gated AI audio model.
sources.exclude_reason: It sits behind a community licence whose revenue threshold was not read.

sources.name: Storyset
sources.holds: Illustrations from the Freepik group.
sources.exclude_reason: It needs credit or payment, and bars collections and robots.

sources.name: Subtle Patterns
sources.holds: Background tiles under an unnamed Creative Commons version.
sources.notes: The Creative Commons version is not named.

sources.name: Suno
sources.holds: Hosted AI music on paid plans.
sources.exclude_reason: It has no public API, and its free plan is non-commercial.

sources.name: Tabler Icons
sources.holds: More than 6,000 open icons.
sources.notes: A hand-picked subset is the bundling plan.

sources.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
sources.holds: Public domain artworks from The Met.
sources.notes: Use API v1.1. The old search route was retired on 2026-10-01.

sources.name: three.js
sources.holds: The standard 3D library for the web, for true 3D scenes.
sources.notes: Pinned in the renderer package when used. Example assets vary, so check each.

sources.name: transition.css
sources.holds: CSS clip-path transitions.

sources.name: transitions.dev
sources.holds: A custom-licensed collection of interface transitions.
sources.exclude_reason: Its licence bars publishing a substantial part as a competing motion pack, which is why 16 HyperFrames ports are refused too.

sources.name: Transparent Textures
sources.holds: 397 numbered background patterns.
sources.exclude_reason: No licence is stated anywhere on the site.

sources.name: Tripo
sources.holds: Hosted 3D generation.
sources.notes: Its official pages turned away our read and secondary sources conflict, so read the terms before using it.

sources.name: TubeLab
sources.holds: YouTube and Shorts research with an API on its Pro plan.
sources.notes: Best runner-up for transcripts. Its terms address returned 404.

sources.name: Twemoji
sources.holds: A widely used emoji set, kept going by its community.

credit.template: Graphics by the Twemoji contributors, CC BY 4.0

sources.notes: Graphics need credit. Code is MIT.

sources.name: Uiverse Galaxy
sources.holds: Thousands of community CSS elements.
sources.notes: Patterns only. Last pushed in September 2024, and the site blocked our read.

sources.name: unDraw
sources.holds: Popular open-style illustrations under a custom licence.
sources.exclude_reason: Its licence bars packs, adding its art to an app, integrations, scraping and AI.

sources.name: Unsplash
sources.holds: Popular free stock photos.
sources.exclude_reason: Its API guidelines call for non-automated use and hotlinking, which an agent tool cannot honour.

sources.name: Uppbeat
sources.holds: Music with a small free allowance.
sources.exclude_reason: Its terms page refused every read, so nothing could be verified.

sources.name: useAnimations
sources.holds: Micro-animated icons for React.
sources.notes: Would need a port to a seekable clock.

sources.name: Vecteezy
sources.holds: Stock photos, video and vectors with a paid API.
sources.notes: Its free tier needs credit, and its terms say you may not download or stockpile.

sources.name: Videvo
sources.holds: A former stock site that now redirects to Freepik.

sources.name: vidIQ
sources.holds: YouTube and Instagram analysis through an official connector.

sources.name: ViewStats
sources.holds: YouTube analytics with a costly business API.
sources.exclude_reason: Its terms ban data mining and robots.

sources.name: Wikimedia Commons
sources.holds: Openly licensed media, with a licence on every file.

sources.name: world-atlas

sources.name: World Bank data

sources.notes: The JSON API works. Its licence page was not read.

sources.name: YouTube Data API
sources.holds: Official public video data, on your own key.

sources.exclude_reason: Its licence page turned away every read. One search snippet says it bars AI training.
